title: Auth direct sign-in: an afterSignOut option so hosted sign-out returns through the identity provider (objectstack#34168 item 3, not shipped; blocks cloud#4471)
body:
repo:cloud#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbYK6SZCmyzbGnrvmkk

**Carry-over from objectstack#34168, item 3.** It was added to that card's scope in comment 6902780898. objectstack#34168 closed as completed after PR #34265, which shipped items 1 and 2, the refusal reason and the client name. Item 3 did not ship. At `main` `b1da9f55db` there is no `afterSignOut` in `plugin-auth`, the spec or the Console; the cloud#4471 build thread checked this. cloud#4471 (p1) is held open on this card for its sign-out step.

## Ask

Add a direct sign-in option `afterSignOut: 'hold' | 'identity-provider'`.
- The default is `'hold'`, today's behaviour under the objectstack#33183 sign-out ruling 6879236460.
- Under `'identity-provider'`, the Console's sign-out `callbackURL` is the direct door `/api/v1/auth/sign-in/direct` instead of `/login`. The post-logout return then goes back through the identity provider's sign-in page.
- There is no loop: the provider's session has already ended, so the provider shows its own sign-in page.

## Done when

A test pins both values:
- under `'hold'`, sign-out lands on the held sign-in page, as today;
- under `'identity-provider'`, the sign-out callback is the direct door.

## Why

cloud#4465 rulings 8 and 10: on a hosted environment, after sign-out the person lands on the cloud sign-in page, and no environment sign-in page is kept. Once this ships in a release the cloud pins, cloud sets `'identity-provider'` and registers the direct door as a post-logout redirect URI. No cloud response rewrite is built in the meantime.

## Related

objectstack#34168 (closed; items 1 and 2 shipped in PR #34265), cloud#4471, cloud#4465.
